title: Case E — Niigata district
summary: Real district in Niigata at 1:250, before and after a 60 m high-rise and two 18 m mid-rises; pedestrian-height velocity ratio (thermistor), 16 wind directions.

configuration.district: Niigata City urban area near the Shinano River; dense low-rise stock (median top 6 m, max 30 m)

states.bc: before construction (sites of A, B, C empty)
states.ac: after construction of A (60 m high-rise), B and C (18 m mid-rises)

configuration.measurement_height_note: 2 m full scale = 0.008 m model scale
configuration.normalisation: velocity ratio = mean scalar speed at 2 m / inflow velocity at 15.9 m (the Niigata meteorological station height); U(15.9 m) = 0.504531 x UR = 3.935 m/s with UR = 7.8 m/s at ZR = 250 m
configuration.instrument: thermistor anemometer, 100 Hz, 60 s per point, mean scalar wind speed

frame.origin: centre of the reproduced area, ground plane
frame.wind_direction_rotation: Meteorological: the compass name is the direction the wind comes FROM (N = 0 deg blows toward -y, E = 90 deg toward -x), clockwise from north. This case keeps its geographic frame instead of '+x along the wind' because the district is real and its coordinates are the data's.

inflow_fit.method: the workbook publishes z/ZR, U/UR, k/UR^2 with ZR = 250 m, UR = 7.8 m/s and epsilon = Cmu^0.5 k dU/dz (Cmu = 0.09); de-normalised to full-scale metres and m/s here
inflow_fit.log_law: does not fit: kappa = 0.41 fits reach 5.3-9.4 % max error over the relevant height range and overshoot U(15.9 m) by 4-7 %
inflow_fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ

gotchas: The velocity ratio is normalised by the inflow velocity at 15.9 m (= 3.935 m/s), NOT by U_H and NOT by UR = 7.8 m/s. A prior Eddy3D comparison in the folder divided by the wrong reference and came out low by a factor of 2.048 (FAC2 0.338 -> 0.863 once rescaled, R unchanged at 0.661).
All 2560 published ratios are integer multiples of 0.0198204 (55 distinct levels): the data's own resolution is +/-0.0099, 3.1 % of the median value and about 10 % at the lowest points.
The readme describes AF_caseE.csv, RS_caseE.csv and BD_caseE.stl, but this repository holds only the .3dm, .ghx, .xls and the MP drawing; everything here is extracted from the workbook and the 3dm.

case-e.3dm is FULL-SCALE metres (MP_caseE.png is drawn at model scale, +/-0.8 m). Use layers 'buildings' (5,015 meshes, before construction) and 'buildings_new_construction' (3 prisms); exclude the map plate on the Japanese-named general layer, the terrain plates (the site is flat) and 'probes'.

Do not take the measurement coordinates from the 3dm's 'probes' layer: its 80 spheres sit a median 2.31 m (max 21 m) from the workbook's points, which are authoritative (all 80 fall in open space, min 0.83 m from a building edge).

The measured quantity is a scalar (thermistor) speed; a RANS |U| is biased low against it in a dense canopy. The construction signal (ac - bc) is largest for SW (mean |d| 0.2155) and smallest for SSE (0.093).
citation_requested: Tominaga, Y. et al. (2008). AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings. JWEIA 96, 1749-1761. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2008.02.058
